title: New video shows suspect shooting high-powered rifle in deadly Crestview standoff - NewsBreak
text:
By Hannah O’Gara ,
59 minutes ago
OKALOOSA COUNTY, Fla. (WKRG) — Okaloosa County Sheriff Eric Aden walked through what led up to the standoff in Crestview, including days earlier, when an employee of Richbourg School called in to report gunshots fired from Antonio Haner’s home on Alabama Street, just across from the high school.
Powerball jackpot reaches $1 billion as Gulf Coast hopefuls dream big “Haner was accused of shooting rounds in his backyard, close proximity to the school and neighborhood residents,” said Sheriff Aden.
Deputies were serving the warrant early Saturday morning when the Sheriff said Haner refused orders to come out and fired a shotgun and high-powered rifle at an armored vehicle.
Another armored vehicle moved in and pinned Haner against the home.
Sheriff Aden said Haner displayed signs of mental illness, as Haner’s wife stated he believed he was called upon to shoot the school.
“She says he believed he worked for the CIA and he was going to shot up the school,” said Sheriff Aden. “Says she personally doesn’t have an opinion that he wouldn’t shoot up the school, but he told her the government was telling him to shoot up the school.”
​First responders provided aid to Haner, but he was pronounced dead at the hospital.
